title: JANUS Tear Policy and Representation Frontier

problem_after_previous_attack.falsified: Every formula's full residual-state space has a polynomial continuation-complete Tear quotient.
problem_after_previous_attack.surviving_question: Can one explicit deterministic policy visit only polynomially many selected states and always recover a SAT witness or an UNSAT certificate?

attack_results.target: all policy orders behave like the C020 equality counterexample

attack_results.target: polynomial payload size implies polynomial state count
attack_results.reason: The torus column Tear needs 2m-1 bits but ranges over 2^(2m-1) extendable states.

attack_results.target: large frontier width proves the instance hard for every algorithm
attack_results.reason: Odd-charge Tseitin has a linear global affine certificate and is polynomial-time solvable.
The algorithm must choose order, decomposition, representation, interface certificates and witness recovery in polynomial total work.

new_missing_theorem.title: Universal Tear Policy and Representation Selection Theorem
new_missing_theorem.statement: For every CNF F of length L, a deterministic polynomial-time procedure selects an exploration order, semantic module decomposition, proof representation, interface Tears and witness-recovery annotations whose total visited states and total work are polynomial in L.
failure_modes_to_cover: bad decomposition: connected C019 neutral glue
bad proof language: toroidal CNF sweep versus affine certificate
exponential count of small Tear signatures
new_missing_theorem.conditional_consequence: A construction proves SAT in P and therefore P=NP.

claim_boundary: This addendum identifies an exact affine policy-width resource and representation sensitivity. It proves neither P=NP nor P!=NP.
